extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users learning TikZ (users wanting to create graphics via TikZ coordinates, loops, and intersections)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for using TikZ to compute and manipulate coordinates and path intersections (loops, coordinate arithmetic, partway/distance/projection modifiers, and the intersections library). Includes syntax, examples, and common idioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements / libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Load the calc and intersections TikZ libraries (\usetikzlibrary{calc} and \usetikzlibrary{intersections}); other features are loaded by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter’s examples assume these libraries; the calc library enables coordinate arithmetic and $...$ coordinate expressions, and the intersections library finds intersection points and provides name path / name intersections keys. Source code is provided at the chapter GitHub link for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: \foreach basic syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \foreach variable in {list of values} {commands}; variable must start with a backslash and acts like a macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may omit braces for a single command. The variable name conventionally uses \i, \j but any name starting with backslash is allowed. Use this to repeat commands rather than copy/paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value list patterns and auto-filling in \foreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists may use the '...' notation to auto-fill numeric or alphabetic sequences (e.g., 1,...,10 or 2,4,...,10 or A_1,...,F_1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auto-filling works with fractional steps (0.1,0.2,...,1). When more values are specified TikZ computes the difference and fills accordingly. Examples: \foreach \i in {-3,...,3} and \foreach \i in {10,20,...,360}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple loop variables / value pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: \foreach can take multiple variables separated by slashes, e.g., \foreach \i/\j in {A/1,B/2,C/3} {commands}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want paired or tuple values per iteration (e.g., alphanumeric labels). You can nest \foreach loops for more complex repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using \foreach inside a single path
rubrics_metrics.description: You can place \foreach inside a single drawing path to build many subpaths within one path, enabling composite fills and even-odd fills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \filldraw[even odd rule] \foreach \i in {10,20,...,360} { (\i:1) circle (1) }; Using a single path lets you apply filling rules (even-odd) across all subpaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using \foreach outside TikZ (pgffor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The \foreach macro is defined in the pgffor package and can be used in LaTeX without loading TikZ by loading pgffor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load \usepackage{pgffor} to use \foreach in non-TikZ contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate arithmetic with calc library ($...$)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place computed coordinates using $(...)$ expressions. Inside $...$ you can add, subtract, and scale coordinates: e.g., $(A)+(B)$, 2*(A), sqrt(3)*(2,2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap the whole coordinate expression in parentheses: \coordinate (B) at ($(A)+(1,0)$); Note nesting of parentheses and $ symbols; complex math expressions are allowed but may require extra braces to disambiguate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar coordinates inside arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: Polar coordinates (angle:radius) can be used within arithmetic expressions, e.g., $(A)+(60:1)$ or (\i:1) for rotated points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine with addition/subtraction or scaling to create rotated/offset coordinates; useful for symmetric constructions like equilateral triangles or rotated circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling coordinates with '*' factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix a coordinate name or literal with a numeric factor and * to scale it, e.g., 2*(A) or sin(60)*sqrt(2)*(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factor may be a numeric literal or a math expression; rarely needed but available for precise computed placements, as in \coordinate (D) at ($sin(60)*sqrt(2)*(A)+0.5*(60:1)$);

rubrics_metrics.name: Partway modifier (factor) — (A)!factor!(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (A)!factor!(B) to get a point on the line AB: factor between 0 and 1 chooses an interior point (0.5 midpoint), negative or >1 values extend beyond the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor behaves like a fraction of the distance from A toward B: (A)!2!(B) is twice the distance from A in direction of B. Useful for midpoints and proportional placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance modifier — (A)!<dimension>!(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of a factor, a physical dimension can be used: (A)!1cm!(B) is the point on AB at distance 1cm from A toward B; negative dimensions go the opposite way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when absolute lengths are required rather than proportions. Example: (A)!-1cm!(B) lies on the line AB but on the other side of A at 1cm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection modifier — (A)!(C)!(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (A)!(C)!(B) to compute the orthogonal projection of C onto the line through A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The projection need not lie between A and B. You can chain projections with further calculations, e.g., drawing a dotted line from C to ($(A)!(C)!(B)$).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding an angle to modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix the second coordinate with an angle 'angle:' in partway/distance/projection modifiers, e.g., ($(A)!0.5!60:(B)$) rotates the line AB by 60 degrees around A then applies the modifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines rotation and partway/distance/projection in a single expression. Example: \filldraw ($(A)!0.5!60:(B)$) circle (0.03);

rubrics_metrics.name: Use curly braces to encapsulate math expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: When math expressions could confuse the parser (e.g., nested parentheses), encapsulate them in { ... } inside coordinate expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw ($(A)!0.5!(B)+(0,{sqrt(3)/6})$) circle({sqrt(3)/6}); Braces prevent the parser from misinterpreting function parentheses as coordinate delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting iterations with count option in \foreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the count option to create an iteration counter: \foreach \i [count=\j] in {values} {commands} makes \j run 1..N (or start from a custom value using 'from').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \j to index positions, labels, or for calculations based on iteration number. Example: \foreach \i [count=\j] in {A,...,Z} { ... }.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating loop variables (evaluate option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use evaluate=\i as \macro using <formula> to compute numeric values from loop variables for use inside commands; evaluate=\i alone will replace \i with its evaluated value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: evaluate=\i as \c using 20*\i to produce a color value; evaluated macros can be used for sizes, colors, or coordinate math inside the loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remembering previous loop value (remember option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use remember=\i as \macro (initially <value>) to retain the value of \i from the previous iteration in \macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to connect consecutive iterations (e.g., drawing segments between current and previous point). Provide an initial value for the first iteration when no previous value exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersections library: name path and name intersections
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare paths with name path=<name> (or name path global) and use name intersections = {of = path1 and path2, ...} to create named intersection coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intersections library will generate coordinates named intersection-1, intersection-2, etc., or a user prefix via name=. Useful to place nodes/arrows at intersection points without manual algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: name intersections suboptions: of, name, total, by, sort by
rubrics_metrics.description: The name intersections key accepts suboptions: of (specify path names with 'and'), name (prefix for intersection coordinates), total=\macro (stores the number of intersections), by (explicit names list), and sort by (path name used to sort intersection order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use total to iterate through intersections in a loop (e.g., \foreach \i in {1,...,\max}). Use by to assign friendly names (a,b,c). Use sort by to set deterministic ordering (e.g., counterclockwise along a circle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sorting and numbering of intersection points
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ finds intersections in its algorithmic order but you can sort them by specifying a reference path with sort by, and provide a name prefix to number them as prefix-1..prefix-N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: name intersections = {of = triangle and circle, total=\max, name=c, sort by = circle} yields c-1..c-\max sorted along the circle path (counterclockwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual/graphic idioms: even-odd rule and shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine path-construction techniques with graphic options like even odd rule for complex fills and shading=ball for shaded circles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \filldraw[even odd rule] ... to get alternating fills for intersecting circles; \draw[shading=ball] to create shaded spheres. Use these stylistic options with computed coordinates for attractive results.
